title: Drying Completion and the Early Equipment Removal Release (Water Damage Mitigation)
content:
Drying on a Water Damage Mitigation job ends in one of two recorded ways, and the Early Equipment Removal Release is the customer's own instrument for the second.

## Terms
The job must be in drying status when an Early Equipment Removal Release is signed. Drying ends either when the logged readings of every affected material reach the dry standard, recorded as dry standard met, or when the customer signs an Early Equipment Removal Release and the equipment is pulled, recorded as customer release. The release is the customer's own decision and signature: it acknowledges that materials were not dry and that the company gives no warranty against secondary damage such as mold growth. A job whose release signed date is filled can only complete with drying outcome customer release. Equipment days are billable through the drying complete date under either outcome.

## The two outcomes side by side
| | Dry standard met | Customer release |
|---|---|---|
| What ends drying | logged readings of every affected material reach the dry standard | the customer signs an Early Equipment Removal Release and the equipment is pulled |
| Whose decision | the drying log | the customer's own decision and signature |
| Acknowledgement | — | materials were not dry; no warranty against secondary damage such as mold growth |
| Equipment days billable | through the drying complete date | through the drying complete date |

## Points of judgement
- A release can be signed only while the job is in drying status.
- Once a release signed date is on the job record, the only drying outcome the job can complete with is customer release.
